description: A FAIR generalizable workflow framework for multi-domain scientific time-series analysis

modules.name: DataIngestion
modules.label: Data Ingestion
modules.description: Domain-adaptive ingestion that normalizes raw sensor archives into a standardized time-series DataFrame (timestamp, elapsed_s, numeric channels). Each domain is handled by a pluggable DomainAdapter implementing the shared interface.

inputs.name: raw_files
inputs.description: Raw sensor archive (SCOTTI v2 CSV, MIT-BIH CSV, Jena Climate CSV)

inputs.name: adapter_config
inputs.description: Domain adapter parameters (target_hz, session_minutes, year, etc.)

outputs.name: clean_df
outputs.description: Standardised time-series with timestamp, elapsed_s, and sensor channels

outputs.name: adapter_meta
outputs.description: Adapter name, channels, native_hz, session length

assumptions: Each domain has a unique raw format handled by its DomainAdapter
All adapters return a DataFrame with timestamp (datetime) and elapsed_s (float)
Downsampling is domain-specific and configured via the adapter

config_params.name: target_hz
config_params.description: Target sampling rate after decimation (ECG: 50 Hz, Climate: none, Satellite: 1 Hz)

config_params.name: session_minutes
config_params.description: Session duration in minutes for ECG records

config_params.name: year
config_params.description: Calendar year to extract for Climate domain

config_params.name: months
config_params.description: Start/end months for Climate slice

modules.name: QualityAssessment
modules.label: Quality Assessment
modules.description: Domain-agnostic sensor quality audit: NaN rates, stuck-channel detection, timing regularity, per-channel z-score flagging, and linear trend detection on selected channels. Outputs a machine-readable JSON quality report.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Domain quality-assessment config (thresholds, expected dt, trend channels)

outputs.name: quality_report
outputs.description: Per-channel quality metrics and summary flags

assumptions: Stuck sensor: <= 3 unique values in a channel across the full session
Z-score flag threshold: configurable per domain (default 3.0 sigma)
Timing gap threshold: expected_dt * gap_multiplier (domain-specific)

config_params.name: stuck_unique_max
config_params.description: Maximum unique values for a channel to be flagged as stuck

config_params.name: zscore_threshold
config_params.description: Sigma threshold for per-channel z-score flagging

config_params.name: expected_dt_s
config_params.description: Expected sample interval in seconds (null = auto-estimate from median dt)

config_params.name: gap_multiplier
config_params.description: Multiplier over expected_dt_s to define a large timing gap

config_params.name: trend_channels
config_params.description: Channel names to run linear trend regression on

modules.name: FeatureEngineering
modules.label: Feature Engineering
modules.description: Builds a multi-dimensional feature matrix from the clean time-series. Nine feature families per channel (when session >= 3x window): (1) raw value, (2) first-order difference, (3) rolling mean, (4) rolling std, (5) rolling skewness, (6) rolling excess kurtosis, (7) zero-crossing rate, (8) spectral entropy, (9) dominant frequency (Hz). Plus a sample-interval timing feature (dt_sample).

inputs.name: channels
inputs.description: Sensor channels to engineer features over

assumptions: Rolling statistics are only computed when session length >= 3 * window
NaN values are forward-filled then backward-filled before feature extraction
Window size should be tuned per domain (ECG: 100 samples, Climate: 24 samples, Satellite: 15 samples)

config_params.name: window
config_params.description: Rolling window size in samples

config_params.name: channels
config_params.description: Channel subset (null = all channels from M1)

modules.name: SemanticAnnotation
modules.label: Semantic Annotation
modules.description: Maps ML detector evidence (feature importances, anomaly scores) and feature names to domain OWL ontology classes. Produces a SPARQL-queryable knowledge graph in RDF/Turtle and GraphML. In core mode, edges encode feature-class membership; in use-case mode, all five detector results are aggregated — IsolationForest importance-weighted edges plus per-detector performance nodes (AUC-ROC, F1, recall) and consensus evidence edges.

inputs.name: ml_results
inputs.description: ML evaluation results from E2 (optional; enables importance-weighted edges)

outputs.name: kg_graphml
outputs.description: Knowledge graph in GraphML for visualization

outputs.name: if_interpretability_report
outputs.description: Human-readable IsolationForest feature importance report listing top-N features with importance scores and ontology class mappings

assumptions: Feature names are matched to OWL class local names by prefix substring
IsolationForest feature_importances_ are used as edge weights (use-case mode only)
Ontology local names follow the domain-specific naming convention

config_params.name: ontology_path
config_params.description: Path to domain OWL file

config_params.name: min_importance
config_params.description: Minimum feature importance to include edge in KG

modules.name: ProvenanceExport
modules.label: Provenance Export
modules.description: Records one prov:Activity per M1-M4 module execution with wall-clock timestamps, input row counts, output file paths, and parameter values. Serialises the complete PROV-O/ProvONE trace to RDF/Turtle.

outputs.name: provenance_ttl
outputs.description: Complete PROV-O/ProvONE provenance trace for the run

assumptions: Timestamps are UTC ISO 8601
SHA-256 checksums are optional (disabled by default for speed)
One prov:Activity per module execution per domain session

config_params.name: output_path
config_params.description: Output Turtle file path

config_params.name: sha256_inputs
config_params.description: Compute SHA-256 checksums for output file entities (always-on; stored as telwf:sha256 in provenance Turtle)

modules.name: FaultInjection
modules.label: Fault Injection
modules.description: Injects synthetic faults into clean sessions to produce labelled evaluation variants. Fault morphologies are drawn from domain-specific taxonomies. A three-tier difficulty system scales amplitude, duration, and channel spread simultaneously to avoid single-axis separability (Wu & Keogh 2022). Part of the anomaly detection use case only; not part of the reusable core.

inputs.name: n_variants
inputs.description: Number of random variants per (type, tier) pair

outputs.name: injected_csvs
outputs.description: One CSV per (fault_type, tier, variant) labelled with anomaly start/end

outputs.name: label_csvs
outputs.description: Corresponding label files with start_idx, end_idx, severity

outputs.name: injection_summary
outputs.description: Summary table of all injected variants

assumptions: Tier 'easy': amp=1.45x, dur=0.30x session, spread=1.25x channels
Tier 'medium': amp=1.05x, dur=0.95x session, spread=1.00x channels
Tier 'hard': amp=0.72x, dur=1.55x session, spread=0.70x channels
All randomness flows from a seeded generator chain for bit-identical reproducibility
Fault window is placed in the second eighth of the session to ensure training data precedes it

config_params.name: tiers
config_params.description: Difficulty tiers to generate

config_params.name: n_variants
config_params.description: Variants per (fault_type, tier) pair

config_params.name: seed
config_params.description: Master random seed

modules.name: AnomalyDetection
modules.label: Anomaly Detection
modules.description: Trains five ML detectors on the first 60% clean prefix; evaluates on injected suffix. Detectors: ZScore (MAD-robust), RobustRollingZScore (CUSUM), IsolationForest (rotation ensemble), Autoencoder (multi-scale MLP), LOF (density-based novelty). Threshold strategy: EVT/POT GPD calibration for density detectors; 99th-pct for statistical detectors. Part of the anomaly detection use case only; not part of the reusable core.

inputs.name: X_clean
inputs.description: Feature matrix of clean session (M3 output)

inputs.name: injected_dir
inputs.description: Directory of injected CSV files (E1 output)

inputs.name: files_generated
inputs.description: List of (tag, tier, variant) tuples from E1

outputs.name: ml_metrics_by_tier
outputs.description: Aggregated metrics by tier and detector

assumptions: Training uses the first 60% of the clean session (train_frac=0.60)
Threshold is the 99th percentile of clean training-set anomaly scores
IsolationForest uses a 3-member rotation ensemble to reduce axis-alignment bias
Autoencoder uses dual sequence lengths (8 and 16) with denoising sigma=0.06
LOF uses novelty=True mode -- fitted on clean data, evaluated on test data
EVT calibration requires >=10 exceedances above 90th-percentile pre-threshold

config_params.name: train_frac
config_params.description: Fraction of clean session for training

config_params.name: threshold_pct
config_params.description: Percentile of training scores for threshold (statistical detectors)

config_params.name: threshold_strategy
config_params.description: Threshold calibration: percentile | evt_for_density (GPD POT for IF/LOF)

config_params.name: n_estimators_if
config_params.description: Number of trees in IsolationForest ensemble

config_params.name: lof_n_neighbors
config_params.description: Local Outlier Factor neighborhood size

config_params.name: evt_pre_pct
config_params.description: POT pre-threshold percentile for EVT GPD tail fit

config_params.name: evt_exceedance_prob
config_params.description: Target exceedance probability for EVT return level

config_params.name: ae_seq_len
config_params.description: Autoencoder temporal window length

config_params.name: ae_denoise_sigma
config_params.description: Denoising noise standard deviation for Autoencoder
